name: Seraiah
overview: Seraiah was a male figure who returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity, as recorded in Ezra 2:2 and Nehemiah 7:7, where he is also called Azariah. There is no specific tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Seraiah means 'YHWH persists,' 'YHWH is prince,' or 'YHWH contends,' reflecting a connection to the Lord's enduring presence and authority. In Nehemiah 7:7, he is also referred to as Azariah, which means 'YHWH has helped,' emphasizing divine assistance. Both names highlight aspects of God's involvement in his life.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Seraiah was the son of Meraiah, as noted in Nehemiah 12:12. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Seraiah's significance lies in his role as one of the returning exiles to Judah following the Babylonian captivity, marking a pivotal moment in Israel's restoration and covenant renewal. His dual naming as Seraiah and Azariah underscores God's sustaining help and leadership during this period. Though details are limited, his presence in the lists of returning exiles affirms his participation in the fulfillment of God's promises to His people.
